To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

alpha-latrotoxins are large proteins (about 120 kDa) with a modular organization that consists of ankyrin repeats and an amino-terminal domain, that alpha-latroxin binds to two families of neuronal cell surface receptors, neurexin and CIRL, and that alpha-latroxins induce synaptic vesicle exoocytosis by a two step mechanism.
alpha-Latrotoxins bind and activate two different types of cell surface receptors, the neurexins (neuroligins, neurofascins, and latrophilins) and the CLs (CIRL, latrophilins).
alpha-latrotoxins bind to neurexins or CLs to stimulate transmitter release from nerve terminals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of alpha-latroxin and its receptors.
the structure and function of alpha-latroxin and its receptors, neurexin and CIRL.
the structure and function of alpha-latroxin, neurexions and CLs, and how these proteins interact to regulate synaptic vesicle exo-cytosis.

the alpha-latrotoxins are a group of proteins, produced by the venom of the black widow spider Latrodectus, which are capable of inducing the exocytosis (secretion) of vesicles from nerve terminals.
